newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Yakovlev eager to buy Fokker.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Yakovlev eager to buy Fokker.

text.p: Russian plane-maker Yakovlev said on Tuesday it still wanted to buy bankrupt Dutch plane manufacturer Fokker NV and would do so without government financial backing if necessary.

Last year Yakovlev asked the Russian goverment for financial guarantees for the deal which it estimates could cost $200-270 million, but the government has not yet provided them, Alexander Dondukov, chief designer at Aviatsionnaya Korporatsiya Yakovlev, told Reuters.
"We are optimistic and are continuing to look for ways to resolve this task without the goverment's participation," he said.
Yakovlev was looking at three options to complete the deal, he said, but declined to give details.
"Until the Dutch actually reject us we will continue to work on this project," Dondukov said.
South Korea's Samsung Aerospace had been one of the principal suitors to take over Fokker, which went bankrupt in March 1996, but it dropped its bid at the end of last year.
Dondukov said Yakovlev hoped to bring fellow aircraft manufacturer Sukhoi into its plans to buy Fokker, and said Sukhoi chief designer Mikhail Simonov supported the idea.
Officials at Otdelniye Konstruktorskoye Byuro imeni Sukhova (Sukhoi) were not availiable for comment.
Yakovlev is interested in Fokker to shore up its position in the Russian short-range plane market, of which it wants 25-30 percent by the year 2000.

Yakovlev used to be the Soviet Union's foremost designer of military aircraft and still designs naval fighter planes. It also designs passenger aircraft and produced the short-range Yak-40 and Yak-42 models.
Last December Yakovlev, the Tupolev design bureau, Sukhoi military design bureau and helicopter producer Mil set up a financial-industrial group.
The four aircraft producers decided to pool their technology to pull Russia's aviation industry out of its crisis.
